Calibration of a fitted model on data like the real ones

Source: R/fp_calibrate_fit.R
fp_calibrate_fit.Rd

Asks whether the credible intervals of a model would cover the truth in data like the ones it was fitted to. The function simulates datasets from the fit with simulate.fp_occu(), so that they keep the design of the real data (sites, covariates, occasions, verification, recorders) and follow the fitted model, refits each candidate model to every dataset, and scores the coverage and bias of their intervals, as fp_calibrate() does for designed simulations.

Usage

fp_calibrate_fit(
  fit,
  models = list(fitted = fit$formulas$fp),
  reps = 50,
  truth = c("mean", "posterior"),
  prob = 0.95,
  base_seed = 1L,
  parallel = FALSE,
  fit_args = list(chains = 4, parallel_chains = 1, iter_warmup = 1000, iter_sampling =
    1000, adapt_delta = 0.95)
)

Arguments

fit

An fp_occu object: the generating model.

models

Named list of false-positive formulas (or NULL for no false positives) to refit. The default refits the generating model. The occupancy and detection formulas, the recorder effect, and the priors are those of fit.

reps

Number of simulated datasets.

truth

"mean" (default) or "posterior"; see simulate.fp_occu().

prob

Width of the credible intervals.

base_seed

Seeds are base_seed + 1, ..., base_seed + reps.

parallel, fit_args

As in fp_calibrate().

Value

An object of class fp_calibration, as from fp_calibrate(), with a single design cell.

Details

The scored quantities are the occupancy coefficients, the detection coefficients, the intercept of the verified method, the mean false-positive rate over sites (p10_bar, when both the generating and the refitted model have false positives), and the slopes of the false-positive rate in the refitted model. A slope that is not in the generating model has a true value of zero.

The most useful comparison pits the model you fitted against a simpler one. For example, if a model with fp = ~ temp + rh estimated clear effects of the covariates on the false-positive rate, refitting fp = ~ 1 to data simulated from it shows how much a constant rate would bias the occupancy effects at your sample size and verification effort. This answers the question for the fitted structure only: a dependence of the false-positive rate on something you did not measure is not part of the generating model.

Each replicate refits every model, so the cost is that of reps times the number of models fits of the size of the real data. Use parallel, and threads_per_chain in fit_args for large datasets.

See also

fp_calibrate(), simulate.fp_occu()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
sim <- simulate_fp(nsite = 300, nocc = 20, conf_effect = 1.5,
                   conf_cor = 0.7, seed = 1)
m_x <- fp_occu(sim$data, occ = ~ x, fp = ~ x, random_recorder = FALSE)
cal <- fp_calibrate_fit(m_x, models = list(constant = ~ 1, fp_on_x = ~ x),
                        reps = 20)
summary(cal)
plot(cal, parameter = "occ_x")
} # }
